facts.raw_span: A 45-year-old man
history of systemic lupus erythematosus
well controlled without immunomodulatory therapy
a 30 × 20 mm painless, slowly progressive mass on his left forehead over 1 year
excision of a similar frontal bone lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia 2 years earlier
denied headaches or neurologic symptoms
CT scan, the lesion showed a ground-glass appearance with homogenous matrix expansion of the frontal bone
Fine-needle aspiration cytology with immunostaining excluded multiple myeloma (no CD138+ cells)
core biopsy demonstrated diffuse sclerosis, complete bone resorption, and intra-trabecular fibrosis
bone was not uniformly mineralized
findings were reported as suggestive of fibrous dysplasia
preoperative laboratory tests, including inflammatory markers, renal function, and blood counts, were within normal limits
